purpose: Runtime full-city open terrain backgrounds, parchment/cel-animation palette

variants.refinement_prompt: Edit this production full-city ground image with ONE targeted correction: the paving features are MUCH TOO LARGE when viewed close-up in the RTS game. Keep exactly the same full-scene canvas proportions, warm parchment-compatible palette, corner vegetation silhouettes/positions, lighting and overall open-ground composition. Replace ONLY the stone paving material with MUCH FINER-SCALE paving: approximately FOUR TIMES as many slabs per linear distance (about16x more individual paving stones overall), roughly80 to100 small flat pavers across the entire canvas width, evenly scaled across the full image in orthographic overhead view. Each small slab has a smooth quiet matte interior, extremely thin low-contrast pale umber joints, minimal weathering. No large grey rectangular blocks or checkerboard patches; keep the broad overall surface tone warm pale cream-grey and nearly uniform. The material is delicate clean cel-animation hand-painting, not noisy gritty photo cobbles. Do not make larger slabs composed of little cobble patterns; ALL actual slab boundaries must be genuinely small-scale and subtle, not huge highlighted tiles. Keep center empty and entirely flat. No buildings, roofs, bridges, water, walls, rocks, steps, UI, cards or text. Preserve the existing few muted corner leaves exactly; no additional decorative elements. This is a single coherent complete background, not a tile atlas, no grid seam or border.
variants.prompt:
Edit this approved gameplay mockup into a GAME-READY SINGLE COMPLETE TERRAIN BACKGROUND. REMOVE all UI, all parchment bars, all labels/buttons/minimap, all cards/portraits/numbers/selection marks. Paint the environment naturally through those areas to the canvas edges. No interface remains. One cohesive full-city open level ground, not texture atlas, not collage, not separate scenery sprites, no repeated tile motifs. Style matches existing Chinese historical parchment-and-ink UI: premium restrained cel-animation hand-painting, warm ivory and pale greige, muted ochre, desaturated jade foliage, delicate umber linework, very soft matte material and diffuse warm light. Lower ground contrast and reduce tiny cracks by about70 percent relative to reference. Avoid bright saturated grass, dark outlines, realistic gritty stone and busy microtexture. Keep 95 percent of the image quiet continuous FLAT walkable ground, with interesting subtle painted material, never plain placeholder color. Tiny partial foliage/grass silhouettes ONLY along the EXTREME outermost 2 percent of the canvas and a few clipped corners; preserve broad open gaps at the middle of all four edges. No bridge, building, roof, gate, wall, railing, stairs, pond, river, boat, platform, rocks, obstacles or foreground props ANYWHERE. No circle of foliage, no enclosed clearing. All foliage must stay flush at the extreme image boundary, no long shadows into the playfield. Almost vertical orthographic overhead camera, one plane, consistent delicate brush style. No text, border, watermark, diagram, checkerboard or cards. It is a production ground illustration for a larger RTS map; coherent, unobstructed and calm behind cards.
CANVAS: WIDE LANDSCAPE canvas approximately1920x1024, aspect about1.875:1.
MATERIAL: Broad warm limestone paving, thin soft light-brown joints, smooth pale cream-grey slab interiors with restrained hand-painted tonal variation. Sparse muted golden-green leaves only clipped at two or three outer corners, no roof.

notes: Actual output dimensions are recorded rather than requested canvas dimensions.
Each city draws one coherent background once, with aspect-preserving cover cropping. No per-district building/scenery overlays.
Two ground illustrations (stone/earth), each in wide/square composition, shared by21 city profiles with subtle tint/whole-image flips. These are not21 exclusive hand-painted maps.
UI/card layouts and mouse input logic are not baked into these images or modified by the renderer.
Small corner foliage is part of the art, not a collidable or interactive node; opacity and visual safety require runtime screenshot review.
